text: Four relatives want to help. Who has the whole plan?
CareRelay gives a fictional family one shared coordination workspace.
Start with the original messages. The reference date keeps local times in context.
Ministral Three, fourteen billion parameters, reads the source locally through Ollama. The input is synthetic. The inference is real.
Each suggestion includes its source quote. A reviewer checks the task, date, proposed caregiver, and uncertainty before approving. The plan only contains items a person has reviewed.
Maya has a work conflict. The return ride has no driver. Both stay visible.
Robin accepts her pickup. Only she can give that consent.
Now the appointment moves. The reviewer selects the original item and confirms the new time. CareRelay cancels the old record and keeps the replacement. Transport remains a separate decision.
The calendar shows the replacement date, with the original history preserved.
Accepted commitments and open questions stay separate, with evidence.
Approve before sharing. Nothing is sent automatically.

This demonstration ends with five active approved tasks, one accepted responsibility, and two source imports. A model suggestion to cancel transport was rejected because its quote did not support that change. Exact evidence still needs human judgment. This is a local prototype for fictional data, not medical advice or a production household service. The payoff is less reconstructing the chat, and a clearer place to start the next conversation. CareRelay. A little less to carry.
